verdict.rationale: Stripe Issuing ships its own declarative spending controls. These rules block merchant categories, countries, merchant IDs or card presence and enforce per-authorization or monthly limits, so authorization events are declined automatically. Single-use agent cards are also invalidated automatically after use. However, the only automated action is approve/decline at authorization time. Anything broader requires the developer to build their own logic behind the synchronous authorization webhook, which is a building block rather than a rule engine. Missing for 10: a general event-to-action rule engine beyond authorization blocking, rules covering other event types (disputes, funding, card lifecycle), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence, and to set spending limits per authorization or per month.
Cards are automatically invalidated after use.
